strings.name: Confucius
strings.role: Thinker and educator · A central figure in the Confucian tradition
strings.country: China (the state of Lu during the Spring and Autumn period)
strings.summary: Confucius was a thinker and educator of the Spring and Autumn period whose discussions of humaneness, ritual, self-cultivation and political order profoundly influenced East Asian thought. Later followers recorded and transmitted his words and actions in texts including the Analects. His lifespan is traditionally dated to 551–479 BCE. Many biographical details come from later texts, making it important to distinguish historical accounts, subsequent interpretations and legend.
strings.coverageNote: This chronology follows traditional dates and scholarly surveys, rather than a precise career established by modern archival records. Accounts differ on his birth and death dates, offices and travels.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-01.value: Traditionally Zou in the state of Lu, in what is now Shandong
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Names
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Personal name Qiu; courtesy name Zhongni
strings.facts.fact-03.label: Key text
strings.facts.fact-03.value: The Analects was compiled by later followers, not finalized as a book by Confucius himself
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Ethical and political thought
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Explored humaneness, ritual and virtue, considering self-cultivation and the relationship between individuals and society.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Education and transmission through followers
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: His teaching and disciples’ tradition continued through texts such as the Analects, with a lasting influence on East Asian education and thought.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Dies in the state of Lu
strings.timeline.event-01.text: Traditional biographies assign his death to this year; disciples and later followers gradually recorded and compiled his words and actions.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Returns to Lu and teaches in later life
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Traditional accounts describe his return after years of travel, followed by a focus on teaching and transmitting ancient texts.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Leaves Lu and travels among the states
strings.timeline.event-03.text: In a common account of his life, he left Lu with disciples and visited other states seeking opportunities to put his political ideas into practice.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Takes part in Lu’s diplomatic rituals
strings.timeline.event-04.text: Accounts in the Zuo Tradition associate Confucius with ceremonial matters in Lu’s relations with Qi.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Holds office in Lu in traditional accounts
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Later biographies describe him holding office in Lu at about fifty; accounts of his posts and their dates differ.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Born in the state of Lu
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Traditionally dated to 551 BCE; information about his birthplace and family comes largely from texts transmitted by later generations.
